top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards a simple, analysable mechanism: moire interference flattens the bands at a magic twist angle (Bistritzer-MacDonald 2011), and correlated insulators and superconductivity appeared at that angle in 2018, since reproduced by many independent groups. It is a new tunable platform for correlated matter, and a citation limited to the flat band and the existence of the phases does not depend on the unresolved pairing mechanism. The allocation (MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero) maps cleanly on the theory pair and the experimental leader, though Cao and the other 2018 first authors are left out. I rank P001 second: it is the more mature, better settled case with a clean Katori-Ye allocation, and I could vote for it without reservation about its scientific standing, but it is closer to a large improvement of already recognised metrology. Any award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no known collaboration with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye, and I am a field outsider on both slated topics
